data.final_week_advice: Focus on high-yield Unit 4 contextual problems and rapid-fire FRQ practice to solidify weak areas before the exam.
data.summary: This single-week plan prioritizes the student's weak Unit 4 by dedicating the first half to deep contextual differentiation practice. The second half shifts to mixed review and timed practice across all units to ensure broad readiness for the exam.

weeks.focus: Master Unit 4 contextual applications and execute timed mixed review.
tasks: Spend 3 hours on Unit 4: Do 10 free-response questions on related rates and motion contexts, then mark them against the scoring guide to identify specific errors in setup vs. calculation.

Spend 2 hours reviewing Units 1 and 2: Complete a 20-question multiple-choice set focusing on limits and derivative definitions, reviewing any missed questions by re-deriving the limits or derivatives from first principles.
Spend 2 hours on Unit 5: Graph 5 functions and identify all critical points, intervals of increase/decrease, and local extrema, verifying each with the First Derivative Test.
Spend 2 hours on Units 6 and 8: Calculate Riemann sums for 3 different functions and find the area between two curves, ensuring correct setup of the definite integral limits.
Spend 1 hour on Unit 7: Sketch slope fields for 3 differential equations and verify one solution by plugging it back into the original equation.
Spend 1 hour on timed practice: Complete a 45-minute mixed FRQ set covering one problem from each major unit, then grade strictly using the official rubric.
